text:
pagerbot: autodetect alert: gateway 5xx rate exceeded threshold for model redwood/pythia-30b-q8. condition: gateway.5xx_rate >= 5% over 5m. paging #eng-sre and #eng-runtime.

sam (eng-sre): taking pager. seeing spike start 2026-03-22T09:14:56Z. @nina can you join runtime triage? tag @diego for infra.

nina (eng-runtime): on it. pulling runner logs and nvml metrics. initial read: repeated segfaults in optimized attention kernels on long-sequence workloads; OOM cascade on a few runners after restart churn.

diego (eng-platform): infra telemetry shows GPU watchdogs on pool-gpu-c; processes killed by oom_killer and GPU resets on host c-07 and c-08.

maria (support): flagged customers: acct-alpha, acct-omega showing elevated errors in their dashboards. CS contacted them to acknowledge incident.

sam (eng-sre): quick triage: root cause chain appears to be a kernel-level memory indexing bug triggered by batched long-context requests leading to SIGSEGV -> runner death -> 502/504 at gateway due to retries/backpressure.

nina (eng-runtime): log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-22T09:18:03Z] model-runner[pid=22411] ERROR SIGSEGV at 0x7fff6b9a
[2026-03-22T09:18:04Z] kernel: Out-of-memory: Killed process 22411 (model-runner)
[2026-03-22T09:18:06Z] model-runner[pid=22420] INFO restarting
```

sam (eng-sre): executing runbook: inference-5xx-live. mitigation plan in order: 1) remove offending model variant from rotation, 2) route traffic to smaller quant variant, 3) spin up fallback pool, 4) collect cores and traces, 5) consider kernel revert.

diego (eng-platform): cordoning problematic hosts c-07,c-08 for diagnostic collection. running minidump/trace collector now.

nina (eng-runtime): issuing emergency route change to steer new requests away from redwood/pythia-30b-q8 -> redwood/pythia-6b-q2 for hosted customers. command:
```
redwoodctl route apply --src=redwood/pythia-30b-q8 --dst=redwood/pythia-6b-q2 --env=hosted --immediate
```

kiran (SRE): temporarily lowered batch_max_tokens to 1024 for hosted endpoints to reduce kv cache pressure while we assess.

maria (support): notified acct-alpha and acct-omega: they reported spikes in 5xx and increased latencies; both teams asked for ETA and confirmation of data integrity.

eli (product): need immediate SLA exposure numbers and recommended customer messages. any persistent failures or is mitigation covering it?

sam (eng-sre): early SLA calc: window 09:14:56-09:30:12; approx 7.2% 5xx at gateway (~41k requests). no confirmed persisted data loss; retries could have caused duplicated work but not stored-state loss (informing CS to reassure customers).

nina (eng-runtime): analysis update: core dumps show crash inside fused_attention_cuda.cu when seq_len > 4096 and kv_cache enabled with certain batch shapes. hypothesis: out-of-bounds memory write from index computation in quantized codepath.

anita (eng-ml): got cores and repro harness. reproducer passes locally on a dev GPU with same driver version. found missing bounds check when kv_len==0 and multi-batch. preparing patch + unit test.

opsbot: minidump and perf traces uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/6162000011/; diagnostic bundle id diag-6162.

diego (eng-platform): scaled fallback pool by +6 instances and set rollout config to prefer safe-kernel on the fallback. also started draining the cordoned hosts.

nina (eng-runtime): safe short-term option: revert to safe-attention-kernel on fallback pool; compute slower but avoids crashes. propose immediate revert and canary patched kernel later.

anita (eng-ml): patch ETA 20h for PR + unit tests. I agree revert is quickest to stop production crashes; we still need to validate optimized kernel fix.

sam (eng-sre): decision: perform kernel revert on fallback pool and keep routing to smaller model for high-risk customers. executing revert now.

diego (eng-platform): command run: redwoodctl infra set-kernel --pool=hosted-fallback --kernel=safe-attn-2026-03-01

pagerbot: infra job started: job_id=77221 for kernel revert rollout. notifying thread on completion.

nina (eng-runtime): revert completed at 09:46:55Z across 6 fallback instances. monitoring telemetry: no new segfaults in 12m, gateway 5xx dipping to 0.6%.

sam (eng-sre): confirm mitigation status: fallback + routing lowered 5xx to under 1% by 09:55. marking incident as partially mitigated. keeping incident open for post-incident tasks.

maria (support): drafting customer follow-ups and potential credit offers for acct-alpha and acct-omega. requesting error counts per-customer for compensation calc.

eli (product): please include the decision rationale: why we used a smaller model vs full revert first, and the cost-latency tradeoffs for customers.

sam (eng-sre): action items assigned:
- anita: open PR with kernel patch + unit tests (ETA 20h)
- nina & diego: canary plan for patched optimized kernel and metrics to watch (ETA 24h)
- sam: incident writeup + SLA exposure calc (ETA 6h)
- maria: customer comms and credits recommendations (ETA 8h)

pagerbot: incident severity set to sev2. handoff: sam will monitor for next 2 hours. runbook note: add long-context synthetic tests to canary suite.

oncall-rotations: @sam acknowledged takeover for monitoring window.

sam (eng-sre): switching to monitoring mode. final note here: add a synthetic test with >8k tokens and mixed batch shapes to CI to catch this class of bug earlier.

opsbot: incident page created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/6162000011

nina (eng-runtime): leaving final ops note: after kernel revert and routing changes, p50 increased ~25ms for affected traffic but stability restored. will follow up with more telemetry dumps.

sam (eng-sre): end of live-thread. last check 09:58:45Z: gateway 5xx steadied at 0.3% for 15m. moving to post-incident activities and postmortem drafting.
